chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out during a night in which it had drizzled, and he was intending to go to the canopy of the Banu Sa'ida. So I followed him, and there was something that had fallen from him, and he said: 'In the name of God; O God, return it to us.' Then I came to him and greeted him. Then he said: 'Mu'alla?' I said: 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' So he said to me: 'Search with your hand, and whatever you find, hand it over to me.' So I found a great deal of scattered bread, and I kept handing him whatever I found. Then I was faced with a sack of bread that I was unable to carry. So I said: 'May I be your ransom! Let me carry it on my head.' He said: 'No, I have more right to it than you. But come along with me.'

He said: So we came to the canopy of Banu Sa'ida, and we found a group of people sleeping there. He went on tucking the bread — one loaf and two loaves — until he reached the last of them. Then we left. So I said: 'May I be your ransom! Do these people know the truth?' He said: 'If they had known it, we would have shared with them the fine seasoning — and the fine seasoning is salt.'

Indeed, God, Blessed and Exalted, has not created anything except that it has a treasurer who stores it — except for charity, for the Lord attends to it Himself. And my father, when he gave something in charity, would place it in the hand of the beggar, then take it back from him, kiss it and smell it, then return it to the hand of the beggar. A charity given at night extinguishes the anger of the Lord, erases great sin, and eases the reckoning. And a charity given by day yields wealth and increases one's lifespan.

When Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon them both) passed by the shore of the sea, he threw a morsel from his provisions into the water. Some of the disciples said to him: 'O Spirit of God and His Word! Why did you do that, when it was from your own provisions?' He said: 'I did that for an animal from among the animals of the water to eat, and its reward with God is great.'

key_terms.الدُّقَّةُ: Fine seasoning; specifically salt mixed with other spices — the humblest and most basic of condiments, used here to indicate what the Imam would have shared even with non-followers
key_terms.خَازِنٌ: Treasurer/keeper — a divine guardian appointed over every created thing; charity alone has no such intermediary as God Himself oversees it
key_terms.رُوحَ اللَّهِ: Spirit of God — a Quranic title for Jesus (AS), affirming his exalted but created status
key_terms.صَدَقَةَ اللَّيْلِ: Night charity — given in darkness to preserve the giver's anonymity; it has special spiritual merit
key_terms.ظُلَّةَ بَنِي سَاعِدَةَ: The canopy/shelter of Banu Sa'ida — a covered meeting place in Medina where the Ansar gathered; it was here that the dispute over the caliphate took place after the Prophet's death
key_terms.كَلِمَتَهُ: His Word — another Quranic title for Jesus, referring to God's command 'Be' that created him

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the virtue of giving charity at night?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident in which Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) secretly went out at night during drizzle to personally distribute bread to sleeping people at the shelter of Banu Sa'ida — even those who did not follow the truth — demonstrating the universality of charity. The Imam then teaches that God personally oversees charity (unlike all other created things, which have a treasurer/keeper), that his own father would kiss and smell charity before giving it out of reverence, that night charity extinguishes divine anger and day charity increases wealth and lifespan, and that even Jesus threw food into the sea for a sea creature, earning great reward. The hadith addresses Mu'alla ibn Khunays, the Imam's trusted agent in Medina, who witnessed this act of nocturnal generosity and recorded these teachings.
